units.title: 1. NMJ Pathophysiology and Ocular Progression
units.guide:
Myasthenia gravis is an NMJ disorder: autoantibody (B-cell) plus T-cell attack on postsynaptic AChR.
The NMJ figure labels ChAT, V/Q Ca++ channel, AChE, agrin, the active zone and voltage-gated Na+/K+/Ca+ channels; ACh vesicle release binds AChR, Na influx and muscle contraction.
Ocular symptoms are m/c; 15-20% stay ocular (good prognosis) while progressors (maximum first 2-3 years) go pharyngeal then proximal then respiratory; the most crucial period is the first 1 year after ocular symptoms.

units.title: 2. Demographics, Antibodies, Thymus and Classical MG
units.guide:
Bimodal peaking: first peak 20-40 yr with females >>> males; second peak >60 years with males > females.
AChR antibody is specific (85% generalised, 50% ocular); MuSK 10-20% of generalised and 40-50% of AChR-negative MG; LRP4 sits in the double-negative population.
MuSK MG is absent in ocular disease, female-predominant, neck-drop with tongue fasciculations, no thymus involvement and pyridostigmine-refractory. In 80% of seropositive cases 70% have thymic hyperplasia and 10% thymoma; thymectomy in adult-onset generalised MG has very good prognosis. Clinical MG is a pure motor syndrome with diurnal variation, fatiguability and fluctuating UL proximal weakness on repetitive movement. Early-onset classical MG is 65% of cases, females >>> males, 20-40 years, antibodies (++++), HLA-DR3, B8, DR9 and thymic hyperplasia; FSHD has symmetrical ptosis and CPEO (mitochondrial) has ptosis + ophthalmoplegia.

units.title: 3. Presenting Features, Signs and Investigations
units.guide:
Ocular symptoms are m/c: asymmetrical ptosis + diplopia + ophthalmoplegia, binocular diplopia, pupils spared, medial rectus maximal. Limb weakness is 10%; bulbopharyngeal involvement includes fatigue while chewing (masseter — specific for MG), dysarthria and dysphagia, plus expressionless facies and drooped posture.
Examination: peek sign, curtain sign, Cogan's lid twitch, sustained upgaze producing ptosis, unable to count digits 1-10 quickly.
Ice pack (cold improves conduction), edrophonium 2 mg IV and neostigmine 1 mg IM all improve symptoms. AChR antibody is most specific; single-fibre EMG (increased jitter) is most sensitive. NCS: MG has normal baseline CMAP, 3 Hz decremental and high-frequency incremental responses; LEMS has reduced CMAP, variable 3 Hz and >100% high-frequency increment.

units.title: 4. LEMS, Drugs, Treatment and Cholinergic Crisis
units.sec: LEMS, Exacerbating Drugs, Treatment & Cholinergic Crisis
units.guide:
LEMS: antibodies against V/Q Ca2+ channel on the pre-synaptic membrane; paraneoplastic with small cell lung cancer; proximal lower limbs (+), ANS (+++), ocular mild; improves with 3,4 di-aminopyramidine. Notes: Anti-Hu is ganglionopathy; Anti-MA2 and anti-CRPM5 are viral encephalitis.
Drugs that exacerbate MG: aminoglycosides, quinolones, macrolides, magnesium (antacids), d-penicillamine, azathioprine, propranolol.
First attack: pyridostigmine 30-60 mg every 6th hourly. From second attack: initial pyridostigmine, maintenance steroids ± azathioprine. IVIg + plasma exchange for myasthenic crisis, life-threatening MG, severe bulbar dysfunction, refractory MG and planned surgery. Cholinergic crisis is overdose of cholinesterase inhibitors with DUMBELLS.
